message:
Now I understand the fuzzer structure. The input is raw H.264/MVC bitstream data. The vulnerability is a heap-buffer-overflow read in `ih264d_get_bits_h264` called from `ih264d_parse_fgc` which is called from `ih264d_parse_sei_payload`.

The issue is that when parsing the SEI film grain characteristics message, the code reads bits from the bitstream without checking if there are enough bits remaining. If the SEI payload is truncated, the `GETBITS` macro will read past the end of the buffer.

Let me look at how SEI messages are parsed and how the bitstream buffer is set up:

<｜｜DSML｜｜>
<parameter=command>grep -n "ih264d_parse_sei_payload\|ih264d_parse_sei_message\|SEI" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/libavc/decoder/ih264d_sei.c | head -40</parameter>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
